source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide when a length must be measured with smaller equal parts of a unit, instead of only whole units.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: unit length still holds here even though The smaller parts must be equal parts of the same unit interval is missing from the stem — on the item about Decide when a length must be measured with smaller.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The unit length rule also covers this: estimating only to the nearest whole unit, so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide when a length must be measured with smaller.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is unit length because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Decide when a length must be measured with smaller equal parts of a' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: unit length is settled by running 'Locate a decimal or fractional quantity on a ruler or number line by': To place a decimal on a number line, first choose the interval containing it, then divide — on the item about Decide when a length must be measured with smaller.

intelligence.enrichment: When an object ends between two whole-number marks, the unit between consecutive numbers can be divided into equal smaller parts so the length can be measured more accurately; for example, 2 7/10 means 2 units and seven one-tenths.
